x: Harwood, Surrey A.C., and Stansbury, Ranelagh A.C., the eventual winner, were running together at this point, with Mitchell lying third, twenty yards behind.

O'Connor, Poly H., forced the pace at the start with Weatherill and Stansbury, both of South London H., in close attendance Footer, who had for a mile been well in the rear, then came through with a rush and the leaders commenced to draw away from the rest of the field.
After completing a circle round the starting field the leading positions were held by Belton (Surrey A.C.), Cohen (Ashcombe A.C.), Penny, Cook, Stansbury (Ranelagh), and Wills.

The leaders at the finish were very much the same as at the half-way stage, except that Powell had worked into second place and an old rival in Stansbury (Ranelagh H.) had got up from round the first fifteen to finish 5th.
Then along comes Bill, in third position, only 25 seconds behind Stansbury (S.L.H.), who had finished on the shoulder of Forryan (Birchfield).
